description: Take the above-average races ranked by how far their entry count exceeds the average, and return every race whose entry count reaches the 10th-highest entry count. All races tied at the cutoff are included.

b.request: Return all races with above-average constructor result entry counts, ranked by their difference from average, including all races tied at the 10th-highest difference value.
b.sql:
WITH race_counts AS (
  SELECT raceId, COUNT(*) as entry_count
  FROM constructorResults
  GROUP BY raceId
),
avg_count AS (
  SELECT AVG(entry_count) as avg_count
  FROM race_counts
),
races_with_diff AS (
  SELECT rc.raceId, rc.entry_count, ac.avg_count, (rc.entry_count - ac.avg_count) as diff
  FROM race_counts rc, avg_count ac
  WHERE rc.entry_count > ac.avg_count
)
SELECT r.*, rwd.entry_count, rwd.avg_count, rwd.diff
FROM races_with_diff rwd
JOIN races r ON rwd.raceId = r.raceId
WHERE rwd.diff >= (
  SELECT MIN(diff) FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT diff FROM races_with_diff
    ORDER BY diff DESC
    LIMIT 10
  )
)
ORDER BY rwd.diff DESC, r.raceId
b.raw: Return all races with above-average constructor result entry counts, ranked by their difference from average, including all races tied at the 10th-highest difference value.

a.request: Count each race's constructor result entries (`constructorResults` records, linked to the race and its circuit) and total their points, ignoring missing points. Group by race id and circuit country. Among the races whose entry count is above the average entry count across all races, list every race whose entry count is at least the 10th-highest entry count, so races tied at the cutoff are all included. Show the race id, the circuit `country`, the total points, the entry count, and how far the entry count is above the average (unrounded). Sort from the largest difference to the smallest.
a.sql: WITH race_stats AS (SELECT cr.raceId, c.country, COUNT(*) as entry_count, SUM(cr.points) as total_points FROM constructorResults cr JOIN races r ON cr.raceId = r.raceId JOIN circuits c ON r.circuitId = c.circuitId GROUP BY cr.raceId, c.country), average_stats AS (SELECT AVG(entry_count) as avg_entry_count FROM race_stats), high_entries AS (SELECT rs.* FROM race_stats rs WHERE rs.entry_count > (SELECT avg_entry_count FROM average_stats)) SELECT he.raceId, he.country, he.total_points, he.entry_count, (he.entry_count - (SELECT avg_entry_count FROM average_stats)) as difference_from_avg FROM high_entries he WHERE he.entry_count >= COALESCE((SELECT entry_count FROM (SELECT DISTINCT entry_count FROM high_entries ORDER BY entry_count DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 9)), (SELECT MIN(entry_count) FROM high_entries)) ORDER BY difference_from_avg DESC;

c.request: Which are the top 10 races by how far their number of constructor result entries exceeds the average number of entries per race? Look only at races above that average. For each one, give the race id, the circuit's country, the total constructor points scored in that race (ignoring missing points), the number of entries, and the difference from the average. List them from the biggest difference down. Take the above-average races ranked by how far their entry count exceeds the average, and return every race whose entry count reaches the 10th-highest entry count. All races tied at the cutoff are included.
c.sql:
WITH race_entry_counts AS (
  SELECT raceId, COUNT(*) as entry_count
  FROM constructorResults
  GROUP BY raceId
),
avg_count AS (
  SELECT AVG(entry_count) as avg_val
  FROM race_entry_counts
),
above_avg AS (
  SELECT 
    rec.raceId,
    rec.entry_count,
    ac.avg_val,
    (rec.entry_count - ac.avg_val) as difference
  FROM race_entry_counts rec
  CROSS JOIN avg_count ac
  WHERE rec.entry_count > ac.avg_val
),
ranked_races AS (
  SELECT 
    raceId,
    entry_count,
    difference,
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY difference DESC) as rank
  FROM above_avg
)
SELECT 
  rr.raceId,
  c.country,
  SUM(cr.points) as total_points,
  rr.entry_count,
  rr.difference
FROM ranked_races rr
JOIN races r ON rr.raceId = r.raceId
JOIN circuits c ON r.circuitId = c.circuitId
LEFT JOIN constructorResults cr ON rr.raceId = cr.raceId
WHERE rr.rank <= 10
GROUP BY rr.raceId, c.country, rr.entry_count, rr.difference
ORDER BY rr.difference DESC

d.request: Return all above-average races that rank in the top 10 by constructor result entry count including all races tied at the 10th position, sorted descending by difference from average, showing race id, circuit country, total constructor points, entry count, and difference from average.
d.sql: WITH constructor_stats AS (SELECT raceId, COUNT(*) as entry_count, SUM(points) as total_points FROM constructorResults GROUP BY raceId), avg_stats AS (SELECT AVG(entry_count) as avg_entries FROM constructor_stats), ranked_races AS (SELECT cs.raceId, cs.entry_count, cs.total_points, avgs.avg_entries, cs.entry_count - avgs.avg_entries as diff_from_avg, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY cs.entry_count DESC) as rank FROM constructor_stats cs CROSS JOIN avg_stats avgs WHERE cs.entry_count > avgs.avg_entries), max_rank_at_10 AS (SELECT MAX(rank) as max_rank FROM ranked_races WHERE rank <= 10) SELECT rr.raceId, c.country, rr.total_points, rr.entry_count, rr.diff_from_avg FROM ranked_races rr JOIN races r ON rr.raceId = r.raceId JOIN circuits c ON r.circuitId = c.circuitId WHERE rr.rank <= (SELECT max_rank FROM max_rank_at_10) ORDER BY rr.diff_from_avg DESC;
